synopsis: TEMP provides an overarching integrated test plan linking virtual and physical tests to decisions, objectives, data, resources, schedules and acceptance criteria; its IDSK logic runs from decision to evaluation question to required data [f16406, f9549, f16409]. The booklet recommends systems-engineering V&V plus a scaled TEMP-style strategy as the programme’s evidence backbone, with one line per claim recording the decision, evidence, method, comparator, acceptance rule, data, owner and date [f9588, f16413]. Although TEMP is required for major US DoD programmes under November 2020 instruction and January 2017 guidance, a literal defence TEMP would be excessive for this eleven-month programme [f9546, f16412]. This recommendation rests on documented practice rather than demonstrated superiority: comparative outcome studies were not found, and the booklet recommends layering planning methods rather than treating any one as complete [f9556, f9552, f9492, f9420]. Operationally, the plan should reserve four months after prototype arrival for physical measurements and model correlation, then use virtual regression for the large scenario matrix while physical testing targets boundaries and worst cases; it must distinguish reducing physical testing from replacing it for safety credit [f16414, f16415, f16417].
